🎙 Foreign Ministry stresses development of Mazandaran citrus exports to neighboring countries

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry has stressed the need to expand exports of citrus products from northern Mazandaran province to neighboring countries, focusing on the province’s production and export potential.

The eighth meeting of the Foreign Economic Relations Coordination Headquarters this year was hosted by the Foreign Ministry on Tuesday. The meeting was attended by economic deputies from government bodies, officials, representatives of the Mazandaran Chamber of Commerce and private-sector businesses.
​
The meeting focused on developing citrus exports from Mazandaran and examined key challenges, existing capacities and ways to expand shipments of the province’s citrus products to neighboring markets.
​
Twelve Iranian diplomatic missions abroad also joined the meeting by videoconference. Representatives outlined import markets for Iranian citrus in their respective countries and stressed the need to address problems facing exporters seeking to access those markets.
​
Hamid Ghanbari, deputy foreign minister for economic diplomacy, emphasized cooperation among government agencies, provincial authorities and private-sector representatives to improve conditions for citrus exports.

🌍 Iran’s airspace safe for all foreign, international flights: CEO of IAC

📌 Zahedan, IRNA – The deputy minister of roads and urban development and CEO of the Iran Airport and Air Navigation Company (IAC), Morteza Dehqan, has emphasized that Iranian airspace is safe for all foreign and international flights, with all international standards and regulations fully observed.

Speaking to IRNA on Tuesday, Dehqan described the air transport industry as one of the most strategic components of national power in the world, saying that airports and air navigation are key pillars of transport infrastructure.
​
He stressed that Iran’s responsibility is to provide safe services to people and aircraft in accordance with international laws and regulations.
​
Referring to regional interactions, he said Iran exchanges air traffic with 12 neighboring countries, with flights operating through Iranian airspace under international regulations and on an equal basis.
​
Condemning hostile US actions during the recent war, Dehqan said that despite Iran’s membership in the Chicago Convention and the prohibition under international regulations against attacks on civilian infrastructure, the United States directly damaged around 27 Iranian airports.
​
He noted that Iran did not rebuild the war-damaged facilities using traditional methods alone, but upgraded the infrastructure through modern studies and advanced equipment, while meeting its international obligations and making maximum use of the capabilities of domestic experts.
​
Criticizing US sanctions and threats against airlines, Dehqan said Iran continues to comply with all international standards despite the pressure, adding, “Our message to the international aviation community is that Iranian airspace is safe for all flights and they can use this route with confidence.”

⚡️ Army spokesperson says ‘Iranian order’ prevails in Strait of Hormuz

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akrami-Nia says that an “Iranian order” now prevails in the Strait of Hormuz, describing the strategic waterway as Iranian.

Speaking on Tuesday about the recent US-Israeli-imposed war against Iran and the calculations of Iran’s adversaries, Akrami-Nia said they had expected economic problems, public dissatisfaction and regional conditions to lead Iranians to take to the streets against the government if Iran was attacked.
​
He said the Iranians, instead, disrupted those calculations through their active presence in the scene.
​
Akrami-Nia said the aim of Iran’s adversaries was to weaken and overthrow the Islamic Republic, while another strategic objective was to advance plans for a “Greater Israel” in the region. He said Iranians had defended the country’s independence and territorial integrity during the 1980-88 Iraqi-imposed war and had again prevented their adversaries from achieving their objectives during the recent conflict.
​
He said the adversary had expected to surprise Iran with a rapid operation, but had instead been surprised by public participation, the resistance of the Armed Forces and Iran’s defense capabilities.
​
Akrami-Nia said one of the important outcomes of the recent war was the establishment of an “Iranian order” in the Strait of Hormuz, adding that the Armed Forces were committed to maintaining the situation.
​
He said the adversary was seeking through media coverage to portray shipping traffic in the strait as normal, but energy markets and shipping conditions showed the situation was different from before the war.
​
The army spokesman described the Strait of Hormuz as an Iranian strategic asset and said the Armed Forces would defend the country’s rights with strength and determination and would not allow the waterway to be exploited as it had been in the past.

📲 @Irna_en​
